- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, use 10–15 day moving average as baseline for smoothing.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often fails to catch the rebound; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.75 and price <65.
